question: Our API has status values like 'status:active' with special characters. How do I add descriptions and code-friendly names like 'StatusActive'? Do these friendly names change what goes over the wire or just what developers see in code?
ground_truth: OpenAPI doesn't natively support adding descriptions to enum values. Use the `x-fern-enum` extension to add both descriptions and custom names. For each enum value, you can specify a `description` field (which will appear in generated SDK documentation and docs website) and a `name` field (which customizes how the enum appears in generated code). This is particularly useful for enum values with symbolic characters like 'status:active' - you can set the name to something code-safe like 'StatusActive' while keeping the original value for the API. Importantly, the custom names only affect the generated SDK code and documentation - the original enum values are still used over the wire in actual API requests/responses, preserving your API contract. So developers use clean, documented enum names in code (e.g., `Status.StatusActive`) which the SDK translates to the actual API value ('status:active') automatically.
